title: America's Un-American AI Companies
gist: Yaqiu Wang and Nicholas Bequelin argue the US could win the AI race against China by leaning into democratic oversight, rule of law, competition, and open debate, but contend American AI companies are instead aggressively lobbying against accountability and aligning with the state -- undermining the very open-society advantages that would differentiate the US from China; this is a paywalled teaser excerpt.

themes.theme: US AI firms undermine their own strategic advantage

insights.claim: The authors argue the United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society -- democratic oversight, rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate -- but that this won't happen as long as American AI companies aggressively lobby against accountability and align closely with the state.
insights.speaker: Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Positions regulatory-capture and anti-oversight lobbying by AI companies as a strategic liability, not a competitive advantage, in the US-China AI competition -- a framing to watch for in future AI policy and antitrust debates.
insights.quote: The United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society: democratic oversight, the rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate.

insights.claim: Nearly every serious proposal in Washington that could constrain American AI companies runs into the same objection: that restrictions would endanger national security and future prosperity by giving China the advantage.
insights.speaker: Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific rhetorical pattern ('China will win if we regulate') that AI companies use in Washington to block oversight -- a lobbying dynamic relevant to forecasting the odds of near-term US AI regulation passing.
insights.locator: In Washington, nearly every serious proposal

insights.claim: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told a 2025 Senate hearing that the US needs 'sensible regulation' that 'does not slow us down,' exemplifying the industry's framing of regulation as a competitive risk versus China.
insights.speaker: Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: A direct, attributable quote from OpenAI's CEO illustrating industry messaging strategy toward Congress on AI regulation -- a citable data point for tracking corporate lobbying positioning.
insights.quote: sensible regulation that does not slow us down
insights.locator: As OpenAI CEO Sam Altman put it at a 2025 Senate hearing
